reviewerSelfCorrection.what: I missed CX-DR001-D044-T2-B1 — that the MEASURED stage had not been performed for this HEAD — and I missed it twice, returning NOT-SATISFIED-GRADE at turn 1 for an unrelated reason and then SATISFIED-GRADE at turn 2 with stage one still unperformed.
reviewerSelfCorrection.howTheMissHappened: The turn-1 and turn-2 drafts opened with 'Not MEASURED regeneration of the manifests (49/49 and 41/41 still match; no source pin moved)'. I verified the premise thoroughly — I re-derived 49/49 and 41/41 myself at both turns — and then let the premise carry the conclusion. Nothing drifted, so I accepted that the stage was unnecessary.
reviewerSelfCorrection.whyThatWasWrong: D-001's text does not condition the stage on drift: 'regeneration of both manifests at HEAD is mechanical and may run now, recorded as MEASURED', and its staged plan gives it its own commit. The manifests carry a measuredAtCommit field precisely so a measurement is recorded AT a HEAD; at turn 2 that field still recorded the 2026-08-13 route commit, not post-D-044 HEAD. The stage is a recording obligation, not a repair triggered by drift, and I graded the SATISFIED gate open while it was outstanding.
reviewerSelfCorrection.patternAndItsDifference: This is not the same failure as my turn-1 blueprint miss. That one was incomplete verification — I checked that a selector resolved rather than what it resolved to. This one is worse: the subject asserted that a governing requirement did not apply to it, and I treated that assertion as framing rather than as a claim to be tested. Verifying the evidence a subject offers for an exemption is not the same as verifying the exemption.
reviewerSelfCorrection.correctionApplied: When a subject states that a governing rule or stage does not apply, I now read that rule's own text and check the exemption against it before accepting any measurement built on top of it. I applied that here to D-001's two-stage clause and its staged commit plan before accepting that f6ad713 discharges stage one, and I verified the regeneration's content structurally rather than trusting its commit message.
reviewerSelfCorrection.onTheRecord: This is the most consequential error I have made in this protocol. It did not reach the register — Codex caught it and the stage has now been performed — but the reason it did not reach the register is the second reviewer, not my method.

verdictNote: SATISFIED-GRADE. Every blocker raised across three turns is now discharged: my C2-SAT-B1 by retiring both live-standing sentences and adding the condition-1 accounting; Codex's CX-DR001-D044-B1 by naming the blueprint delta under the rule that governs it; and Codex's CX-DR001-D044-T2-B1 by actually performing the MF-8 MEASURED stage at f6ad713. I did not accept that last one on its commit message: I proved structurally that both manifests changed exactly one leaf each, measuredAtCommit, with no pin, selector or execution touched, and then re-derived the entire criterion at the new bytes — 49/49, 41/41, 13 selectors, 6/6 executions with both EP13 stdout digests, 15 claim bindings at zero mismatches. The two stages are now in the order D-001 requires, with MEASURED as its own commit and the SATISFIED re-record as a later independently reviewed file-08-only act. On these measurements that re-record is lawful. My one advisory is carried, unchanged and expressly outside the grade. And the honest reading of this cycle is that I missed the missing stage twice by testing the draft's evidence instead of its exemption; the register was protected by the second reviewer, not by my method.
